end.summary:
• Discussed shared responsibility for keeping school clean, green, and safe.
• Anika identified using dustbins instead of throwing waste on the floor and mentioned bad smells from litter.
• Practised sorting wet waste such as peels and leftover food into the green bin, and dry waste such as wrappers and plastic spoons into the blue bin.
• Discussed compost pits, recycling, oxygen, and mixed-waste disposal.
• The idea that plastic belongs in a compost pit remained at the final check; teach-back was not passed.
end.parentNote: Anika practised everyday school-cleanliness actions and sorting wet and dry waste. They gave examples such as apple peels, leftover food, wrappers, and plastic spoons, and explained that green-bin waste can go to compost while blue-bin waste can go for recycling. A mix-up about plastic spoons going into a compost pit was discussed but was still present at the end. At home, practise sorting a few household items by asking, “Green compost, blue recycle, or neither?”
